metadata.case_name: WONG MAN KIT MICHAEL v. WONG FONG WOON

plaintiff.occupation_before: odd job worker (Woo Sang Construction Co.)

injuries.description: a 4 cm laceration over the left side of the forehead
source: 1) a 4 cm laceration over the left side of the forehead;
injuries.icd_description: Laceration without foreign body of head

injuries.description: a compound fracture of mid-shaft of the left femur
source: 2) a compound fracture of mid-shaft of the left femur; and

injuries.description: a compound fracture of the 1/3rd left tibia
source: 3) a compound fracture of the 1/3rd left tibia.

injuries.description: amputation of the left leg above the knee (after gangrene due to damaged arterial supply)
source: "On 20.3.83 after a traffic accident he was admitted to the United Christian Hospital He suffered a fracture of the left femur, bone of the thigh and a compound fracture of the tibia. The arterial supply to the leg was damaged and the leg became gangrenous and was amputated on 15.4.83. He remained in hospital until September and an artificial leg, or prosthesis was supplied in mid June and he was trained in its use. He reported back in October and his sick leave terminated six months after the accident."
The amputation was above the knee and left a stump which Dr Wedderburn described as "7" long to its margin and 8" to the end of the stump".
injuries.icd_description: Traumatic amputation at level between left hip and knee

manifestations.description: phantom limb symptoms which Dr Wedderburn said usually disappear after two years

He can now walk for about 15 minutes without discomfort after which he has to sit down for one or two minutes rest, or put pressure on the normal leg. He limps slightly but can manage to go up and down steps, taking some rest while going up.

the left leg with the prosthesis on was shorter than the right leg by at least two inches, as a result of which he had to twist his back pushing his right hip upwards and his left leg downward because of which he could not walk normally
In the early stages of the use of the prosthesis the skin of the stump was easily torn and the plaintiff had to treat the wound with alcohol

compared with a normal person, the plaintiff cannot do any heavy work whatsoever that is, moving and bearing weight; he cannot do any work which requires him to move quickly on his legs; as a young man he cannot enjoy himself in activities which young men enjoy like games, and dancing and he will have to look after the artificial leg for the rest of his life

treatments_received: admitted to the United Christian Hospital
prosthesis supplied in mid June 1983 and trained in its use
new prosthesis fitted sometime after May, 1987
treatments_future: replacement of prosthesis of similar type periodically (prosthesis lasts at least four years according to Dr Mao)
maintenance and regular checks on the prosthesis (including travelling expenses)
special socks for use with the prosthesis

losses.description: Amputation above the knee of the left leg
Cannot walk normally; can walk about 15 minutes then needs rest; limps; difficulty going up and down steps without rest

losses.category: Loss of ability to engage in sports and hobbies
losses.description: He used to play football and basketball and went out jogging and fishing. His recreation now is limited to fishing only.
For two months after leaving hospital, he was nursed at home by his mother who had to give up her baby-sitting job which paid her $1,500.00 per month

comparable_cases.injury_description: revised compensation suggested in the guidelines in LAU Che-ping is $180,000 to $225,000
